method: Each box is a fraction of the full photograph (x0, y0, x1, y1; x right, y down), placed by eye on a 10 x 10 grid inside one patch of a single material and checked on the swatch sheet. The tool drops clipped pixels (any channel 250 or more) and keeps the pixels between the 70th and 95th percentile of the box's luminance, i.e. the sunlit faces of stones rather than joints, crevices and self-shadow (a renderer adds its own shading, so the base colour should be the lit face; a first pass at the 15th–85th and then 40th–90th percentiles gave colours darker than the stones' lit faces because rubble walls are mostly crevice), and records their per-channel median sRGB. A surface colour is the median of its sample medians. Boxes that were blown out or lit by low evening sun were dropped after the first pass (kh-qumran-l12-13 ground, kh-qumran-l110 channel, qumran-reference lip). Photographs differ in exposure, white balance and lighting, so the result is a photo-guided base colour for procedural surface art, not a measured ancient surface colour. A dusk photograph (wadi-qumran-pw28412) gave bluish greys and was dropped from the colour samples. Calibration: photographs are exposed automatically while the renderer's lighting is fixed, so raw medians render darker or brighter than the site looks. The atlas therefore uses each sampled colour's hue and chroma (CIELAB a*, b*) and its lightness relative to the other surfaces at the same site, and shifts the site's lightness so that its mean L* equals the mean L* of the earlier hand-tuned palette for the same surfaces. Raw medians are kept as photoMedian with the shift applied (lightnessShift).

gerizim.lichenNote: Reference photographs show clean pale ashlar with only small orange lichen spots (gerizim-ovedc-c24, gerizim-yonger-2018); the earlier dark weathering weight of 0.28 was reduced.

hyrcania.masonryNote: Summit walls survive as tumbled rubble of rough blocks beside stone paving; the reservoirs are cut into pale chalky rock (hyrcania-c-hurkaniatop, hyrcania-c-hurkania-5011).

jericho.masonryNote: Palace walls of rough fieldstone in rough courses, larger roughly squared stones at a corner (jericho-palaces-hasmonean-palace-2013); a mud-brick wall stands beside a plastered stepped pool (jericho-palaces-mikveh). Mud brick is noted but not sampled as stone.

doq.masonryNote: The summit enclosure wall is coursed squared stone close to rough ashlar (doq-ihm-fortress-2, at sunset, used for type only). No ancient masonry was sampled for colour; the stone and plaster colours keep the earlier palette.

samples.note: lower cliff face clear of the caves

bethesda.masonryNote: Pale limestone walls in regular courses with squared faces (jer_bethesda-north-pool-2021, jer_bethesda-pools-dam-2021); Duprez 1970 p. 33 gives the central dam ashlar faces in courses of about 60 cm. Much of the standing masonry is Byzantine and Crusader. Bedrock, soil and plaster keep the Siloam (Jerusalem limestone) palette.

eastgate.masonryNote: Very large squared blocks with fine joints in the lowest visible courses of the gate's outer face (jer_east_gate-exterior-2025-722); smaller squared blocks in regular courses higher on the gate and wall (jer_east_gate-exterior-cemetery-2014). Course height 0.76 m is Warren's 2 ft 6 in for the massive wall (SWP Jerusalem p. 145). No bedrock or plaster is visible, and the only ground sampled was modern gravel in blue sky light, so rock, soil and plaster keep the Jerusalem palette.
